value.subtitle: A euro-and-crypto account — and the release where the entire product turned dark.

hero.alt: akt.io switching from light to dark theme
hero.caption: The switch to dark, announced in-product — prototype recording

sections.heading: Two kinds of money, one balance
sections.body: The account holds euros and crypto at the same time, so the dashboard has to answer “how much do I have” before it answers “in what”. A single total leads, the split follows as cards, and the day’s movement is stated twice — in euros and in percent — because that is how people actually check.

images.alt: Dashboard with total balance, euro and crypto cards and transaction history
images.caption: Total first, composition second, movement in both units.

sections.heading: Market data without the theatre
sections.body: The asset screen holds a price history, a buy, a sell and the tabs that separate market data from your own performance. A chart in a wallet is decoration unless it answers a question, so the line keeps a readable range, a labelled value on the crosshair and timeframes that run from a day to everything.

images.alt: Asset screen with balance, buy and sell actions and price history chart
images.caption: Buy, sell, and a chart that answers a question.

sections.heading: A theme is a system question
sections.body: Dark mode shipped as an event: announced inside the product, with a way to decline and no consequence for saying no. Behind the modal it is design-system work — every token needs a dark counterpart, including chart lines, gradient cards and disabled states, which are precisely the parts of a fintech interface that break quietly when a palette is inverted.

images.alt: In-app modal announcing dark mode with accept and decline options
images.caption: Announced, optional, reversible.
